subject: Strategy flash: competitive snapshot & QBR prep
messages:
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Strategy flash: competitive snapshot & QBR prep

Team — quick leadership-level snapshot ahead of QBR prep next week. This is NOT the QBR slide deck, just a short market signal update so the product and sales workstreams can surface asks and risks. Attached: competitive_snap_v2.pdf

Top signals (high level):
- Aurelia Cloud: announced a new usage tier with 40% lower per-token price on short-sequence inference (<=128 tokens). Public memo this morning. Implication: pressure in price-sensitive segments and reseller deals.
- EdgeIntel (partner/competitor): GA'd a 4-bit quantized variant of a mid-size instruction-tuned model (comparable baseline latency to our light quantized profiles). Early benchmarks show 10–15% latency improvement in 8-token generation workloads.
- Open-source model release: "Orca-XL-lite" forks appeared in the wild; some clouds are packaging it with permissive inference licensing. Potential for quick re-bundling into managed endpoints.

Immediate asks:
1) Sales: Grace — can you flag any active renewals this month where Aurelia or price-led conversations exist? Prioritize two deals for possible credit/discount requests.
2) Product/Serving: Karthik — evaluate whether a temporary price/cost play (short-term promo on short sequences) is feasible without violating unit-economics.
3) Ops: Rishi — compile quick telemetry (7d) on short-sequence traffic mix by customer tier; send by Monday EOD so we can scope impact numbers for QBR.

Goal: surface clear risk/recommendation lines for the QBR slide: — commercial ask (discounts/credits) — tactical product mitigation (bundle/limit) — routing fallback (pin to existing cache profiles).

Markus
VP Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Thanks Markus — useful put. A couple notes from leadership & ops perspective: 
- Please prioritize customer-facing communications only where legal has signed off (we'll loop in Legal/SalesOps if we decide to offer credits).
- For the QBR: we should have three slides: signal, impact (revenue + latency risk), and our recommended mitigations (with owner and ETA).

Grace — if you have >1 renewal flagged, identify which one has an exec sponsor at the customer; those are the highest-priority escalation candidates.

I'll be at the QBR but would like an executive summary deck (2–3 slides) by Tue morning. Rishi — can you confirm timeline for the telemetry note?

Laura Bennett
Chief Revenue Officer

Confirming — I'll pull short-sequence telemetry and attach a 1-page summary by Mon 18:00 PT. Quick preview numbers I'm already seeing in the dashboard sample: ~22% of total token volume is <=128 tokens; for Free/Starter tiers it's ~48%. That could materially change short-seq unit economics if Aurelia picks up procurement momentum.

I'll also grab the last 30-day hit rate for our prefix cache to estimate incremental cost if we need to route to heavier quantized variants.

Will attach: aurelia-price-memo-aug2026.eml (forwarded origin) + short-seq-telemetry-1p.csv (internal).

From: Aurelia Cloud Pricing <pricing@aurelia-cloud.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:00:00 -0400
Subject: Public pricing memo — August 2026 (short-tier launch)
To: partners@aurelia-cloud.com

Hi partners — today we're launching a new short-sequence pricing tier for inference under 128 tokens. Goal is to accelerate consumption for chat widgets and search snippets. Early channel partners will get a trial rate for 60 days.

Public link: https://aurelia-cloud.com/pricing/aug-2026

Aurelia Pricing Team

--
Aurelia: copied FYI as requested. We wanted to make sure your team has this in the thread for QBR swipe material.
observations: Most risk is concentrated in low-MRR, high-volume short-sequence usage where our cache/short-path economics are most sensitive.
EdgeIntel's quantized variant reduces latency on short generation workloads and could be positioned by partners as a performance win for latency-sensitive embedded use cases.
Immediate commercial levers: targeted credits for 2 renewals, temporary short-seq promo, or routing recommendations to quantized variants for non-sensitive customers.
